text:
I applied to 50 jobs and got rejected from all of them.

It felt terrible at first.

But then I realized something:
Rejection is feedback.

I improved my resume, built 2 projects, and kept applying.

2 months later, I got my first offer.

Don’t stop. You are closer than you think.

Most developers focus only on learning.

Very few focus on building.

And that is the difference.

Courses give you knowledge.
Projects give you proof.

If you want to stand out, start building today.

You don’t need 10 programming languages.

You need 1 language and strong fundamentals.

Focus on:
- Data structures
- Problem solving
- Real-world projects

Depth beats randomness every time.

Your first tech job is not about salary.

It is about learning.

Pick a place where:
- You can grow
- You can fail safely
- You can build real things

Money will follow later.

Everyone wants a high-paying job.

But no one wants to go through the boring phase.

Consistency is boring.
Practice is boring.
Learning fundamentals is boring.

But that is what creates results.

Stop comparing your journey with others.

Someone started before you.
Someone has more resources.

Focus on your path.

Small progress every day is enough.

AI is not replacing developers.

Developers who use AI will replace those who don’t.

Learn how to:
- Use AI tools
- Build with APIs
- Automate workflows

Adapt or get left behind.

Your resume is not your identity.

Your work is.

Show your skills through:
- GitHub
- Projects
- Contributions

Let your work speak for you.

If you are waiting for motivation, you will wait forever.

Start without it.

Action creates motivation.
Not the other way around.

You don’t need a perfect plan.

You need a starting point.

Start small.
Improve daily.

Momentum will take care of the rest.
